headline: FOMC MINUTES HAWKISH BUT GOLD HOLDS $3,850 — Markets Signal December Hike Fully Priced; $3,900 Key Resistance Tests Recovery
snippet: The Federal Reserve's October 27–28 FOMC minutes released Wednesday confirmed a broadly hawkish committee, with strong consensus around a December 9 rate hike given October's hot 0.4% CPI print. Despite the hawkish confirmation, gold held near the $3,850 level rather than extending its recent slide to 14-month lows — a potential signal the December hike is now fully priced in. Analysts identify $3,840 as critical support and $3,900 as key resistance; a close above $3,900 would mark the first constructive technical shift for miners since September, while a break below $3,840 opens the path to $3,700.

headline: TRUMP MEETS XI IN SHENZHEN TOMORROW AT APEC — Rare Earth Export Pause Extension at Stake; $15-20x Western Price Gap Signals Supply Crisis
snippet: U.S. President Trump meets Chinese President Xi in Shenzhen on November 19 at the APEC summit, with critical minerals and rare earth export controls near the top of the bilateral agenda. China's existing pause on rare earth restrictions — secured under the October 2025 Busan trade pact — expires January 10, 2027, making this summit the last major diplomatic window before the deadline. Western spot prices for dysprosium and terbium now trade at 15–20x Chinese domestic levels, the widest divergence on record, underscoring the structural urgency behind any extension deal for processors and downstream manufacturers locked out of Chinese supply.

headline: COPPER BOUNCES 1% TO $13,796 AS AI SELLOFF FEARS FADE — Yangshan Premium Near $230/t Record Confirms Physical Tightness Intact
snippet: LME three-month copper recovered roughly 1% to $13,796 per tonne on Wednesday as investor fears around AI capital expenditure cuts eased following strong earnings from AI infrastructure firms; zinc, nickel, and tin also gained across the complex. The Yangshan copper import premium into China — a real-time physical demand signal — held near its record $230 per tonne, reinforcing the thesis that this week's LME selloff was macro-driven rather than a sign of weakening Chinese physical demand. For junior copper developers, the premium divergence provides the most direct evidence that any macro-driven price recovery should be amplified by genuine structural tightness.

headline: FOREMOST CLEAN ENERGY HITS URANIUM IN INAUGURAL DRILL AT TURKEY LAKE — Saskatchewan Basement System Confirmed; Assays Pending
snippet: Foremost Clean Energy (TSX-V) confirmed uranium mineralization during the inaugural drill program at its Turkey Lake project in Saskatchewan on November 17, with elevated radiometric readings intersected across multiple drill holes validating a basement-hosted uranium system in the Athabasca-adjacent corridor. Chemical assay results are pending, so grade and width data are not yet available; results will inform the design of a Phase 2 program. The discovery adds to a cluster of early-stage Athabasca Basin uranium exploration plays advancing on the assumption that spot uranium near $90/lb will eventually close the equity-to-commodity price gap reflected in URNM's year-low levels.

headline: ASX 200 FALLS WEDNESDAY AS MINERS LEAD LOSSES — Global Tech Selloff and Commodity Weakness Extend Bear Market Into November Week 3
snippet: The ASX 200 fell Wednesday with the mining sector leading losses, extending a cross-market selloff driven by continued AI-sector investment concerns, a firm U.S. dollar near 19-month highs, and persistent rate-hike expectations ahead of the December 9 FOMC decision. Lynas Rare Earths dropped 7.4% and broader gold and base metals equities weakened as the sector absorbed the overnight Nasdaq selloff and hawkish FOMC minutes. For ASX-listed junior miners, Wednesday marks the third consecutive week of broad sector weakness — a pattern consistent with investors reducing speculative exposure ahead of a macro catalyst rather than a bottom-forming event.

headline: GOLD BEARS FACE CRITICAL TEST AT $3,840 YEARLY LOW — Forex.com: Next Support $3,700 If Level Breaks; December FOMC Is the Binary
snippet: Forex.com's November 17 short-term gold price outlook identifies $3,840 as the critical yearly low support: a confirmed break opens the path to $3,700 as the next meaningful floor, while a hold above $3,900 resistance would signal the first technical trend shift since late September. The December 9 FOMC decision is framed as the primary binary — a hawkish outcome reinforcing further hikes likely tests $3,840 within days, while any hint of a pause or terminal rate ambiguity is the primary year-end recovery catalyst the gold sector has been waiting for since October's hot CPI reversed the rally from all-time highs.

headline: KINROSS GOLD BOUNCING AHEAD OF THURSDAY DIVIDEND EX-DATE — Class Action Priced Into $12.80 Year Low; Bargain Buying Near Multi-Month Lows
snippet: Kinross Gold (NYSE: KGC; TSX: K) recovered modestly from multi-month lows Tuesday and Wednesday as retail investors moved ahead of the quarterly cash dividend with an ex-date on November 19; a securities class action tied to the September production guidance cut appears fully reflected at current prices near the 52-week low of $12.80, against a year high of $34.17. Analysts describe the Q3 guidance reduction as already priced in and frame the current level as a potential entry point for investors with a view on gold recovering from 14-month lows — particularly if the December FOMC meeting produces any dovish nuance.

headline: 4 GOLD MINING STOCKS POSITIONED TO OUTLAST THE BEAR MARKET — Zacks: Newmont Tanami Cuts AISC 30%, B2Gold Cash-Flow Positive at $3,850
snippet: Zacks Research identifies four gold mining stocks positioned to maintain value through the current bear cycle, with Newmont and B2Gold leading the list. Newmont's Tanami expansion is cited as the key catalyst — expected to add 150,000–200,000 ounces of annual production while reducing operating costs by approximately 30%, giving the stock a credible recovery lever even at current gold prices. B2Gold is highlighted for a clean balance sheet and free cash flow generation at $3,850 gold — both characteristics that distinguish resilient operators from companies now facing genuine viability pressure as gold tests multi-year support.

headline: ASX GOLD EXPLORERS COMPETING FOR MAIDEN RESOURCE IN BEAR MARKET — Stockhead: Funded Contenders From High-Grade Belts Holding Value
snippet: Stockhead identifies ASX gold explorers that are close to publishing a maiden JORC resource estimate, profiling companies with funded multi-hole programs in credible high-grade belts rather than depleted historical corridors. The analysis argues the market is bifurcating sharply in the current bear environment: companies approaching a first resource with the data to support it are holding value or advancing while explorers that lack grade or funding to complete the story are falling further. The piece provides a framework for distinguishing investable exploration-stage risk from speculative exposure that tends to get destroyed in a prolonged commodity price pullback.

headline: HOW TRUMP-XI HISTORY MOVES RARE EARTH STOCKS — Discovery Alert: Every Summit Since 2025 Has Been a Binary Event for ASX and US-Listed Names
snippet: Discovery Alert Australia's analysis of tomorrow's Trump-Xi APEC meeting tracks how every major U.S.-China diplomatic summit since October 2025 has produced a sharp binary move in rare earth equities — with outcomes ranging from a 72% single-day surge in Critical Metals to 15%+ drops when diplomatic progress stalls. The piece argues that the November 19 APEC meeting in Shenzhen is the most consequential summit yet for ASX and U.S.-listed rare earth stocks because China's existing export control pause expires January 10, 2027 — a hard deadline that transforms tomorrow's outcome into a direct read on supply availability for the next 12–18 months.
